title: Keyboard focus is not lost when a dialog closes or a card disappears
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 2 browsers (your dispatcher + a second Admin) · about 20 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders). This user is the dispatcher.
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  • A second browser signed in as an Admin (to deactivate a technician during the test).
  • Technicians (examples): "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", and a technician for this case only, "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Ben Bravo" (the steps call him Ben; step 6 deactivates him). A staff member counts as a technician when, in Settings > Staff > the staff member's edit icon > Edit Staff Member, they are Active, Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customers (used by this case only, each with one contact and one asset): "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept Bravo Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept Charlie Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept Golf Co". The steps and expected results call them by the end of the name ("Alpha Co", "Bravo Co", "Charlie Co", "Golf Co").
  • Work orders (Approved): lead Ana — Alpha Co, Bravo Co; lead Ben — Charlie Co; no lead — Golf Co.
  • The Status filter starts with nothing ticked.
  • Put the mouse aside. From step 4 on, use only the keyboard.
  • The keyboard and focus design is not finished yet (the design shows no keyboard behaviour). Where a step names a key, try Tab, Shift+Tab, the arrow keys, Enter, Space and Escape, and write down which key does what.

Setup

  1. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha" exist and count as technicians at this location (edit icon > Edit Staff Member). To add one: New Staff Member with those settings (at least one Department is required) (e.g. first name "ZZAUTOTEST Ana", last name "Alpha") > Save & Close. Add "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Ben Bravo" the same way (first name "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Ben", last name "Bravo").
  2. Create this case's customers: "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept Bravo Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept Charlie Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept Golf Co". For each: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name > Save; on the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact); then the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  3. Create each work order listed in the Preconditions: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. Move it to the status named: a new work order starts as Estimate (it opens with the New Line form: pick a ready-made line and Save & Close); for Approved turn on Line Approved on its line; for In Progress click Start on the line's Labor row (stop the clock afterwards with Stop > Clock Out); for Review click the line's Complete button, type a Tech Story (fill any missing detail it asks for, e.g. Mileage) and click Complete Line (the List shows "Ready For Review"); for Complete then click Mark Reviewed, enter the VIN if asked and click Confirm Review; for Declined save the line with Line Approved off and click Decline on it (it must be the work order's only line); for Invoiced complete and review it first, then Finance tab > Create Invoice; for Paid, after invoicing, Finance tab > New Payment for the full amount > Make Payment. Set the lead technician before invoicing. Once the work order is Approved, pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page (leave it as Unassigned for an unassigned one). (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Write down each work order number as you create it (e.g. S1-801); the steps call each work order by the end of its customer name (e.g. "Alpha Co"). Use "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Ben Bravo" as Ben.
  4. Sign in as an Admin in a second browser at the same location.
  5. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > List > type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept" in Search — exactly 4 work orders show, all Approved: Alpha Co and Bravo Co led by Ana, Charlie Co led by ZZAUTOTEST F3 Ben Bravo, Golf Co with no lead. If anything differs, correct that work order (status or Lead Technician) before starting.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Keyboard Focus Kept" in Search so only this case's work orders show.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher (tooltip "Board View").
  4. Using only the keyboard, focus the Alpha Co card, open its more-actions menu, open "Reassign lead technician", then close the dialog with Cancel (or Escape). Note where focus is.
  5. Click Status, tick "Approved" only, then by keyboard focus the Golf Co card. In the second browser change Golf Co's status to In Progress, then refresh your board. Note where focus is.
  6. Clear the Status filter. By keyboard focus Ben's column. In the second browser deactivate Ben (Settings > Staff > Ben > Edit Staff Member > Deactivate Account), then refresh your board. Note where focus is.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: when the dialog closes, focus returns to a sensible place (you can see it and keep working without the mouse). Write down where it went.
  • Step 5: after Golf Co leaves the filtered results, focus is not lost. It lands on a visible, sensible element. Write down where.
  • Step 6: after Ben becomes inactive, focus is not lost. Write down where it lands.
  • Where focus should go is not designed yet. Pass if focus is always visible and the keyboard user can carry on. Fail if focus disappears (for example back to the top of the page or nowhere visible).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10054 (Story 11, Keyboard access and focus); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S11-R6, S11-E1, S11-E2, Story 11 user story, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions page 853901313, SQ-15 (Open) and UX-19 (Open). Inline PRD comment by Slavcho Mitrov, 28 Sep 2026, lists what is still open with design. Tech plan (revised 24 Sep 2026) Phase 11.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S11-R6: “Design must define where focus returns after a dialog closes.”
  • S11-E1: “Design must define focus recovery when a work order leaves the filter result.”
  • S11-E2: “Design must define focus recovery when a technician becomes inactive.”
  • Story 11 user story: “As a keyboard user, I want to navigate work orders and their actions so that these controls are usable without a mouse.”
  • Story 11 design line: “keyboard interaction design pending”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.
